kind: perf3 executed CPU/allocation attribution plan; build examples distinguished from execution records
prepared_by: review sub-agent (read-only; no builds, captures or benchmarks run)

harness.why: Same collector that produced docs/evidence/cli-perf2/profiles-{before,final}.json (source report harness/results/perf2/profiles-final/report.json, sha256 7d77d8e1604e...). It runs unprofiled controls first for go-release, rust-release, go-symbolized and rust-symbolized, checks every profiled Rust/Go contract against the first unprofiled Go control, records binary/fixture/meter/tool identities and the source snapshot, and analyzes only after every capture.
harness.not_used: harness/phase7_profile.py only supports PTY/TUI cases (sql-window20000, dense-metrics1000, editor) and needs QuietWindow approval plus symbol-evidence manifests. It has no SQL JSON/text pipeline cases.
harness.summarizer: docs/evidence/cli-perf2/profile_summary.py <report.json> <summary.json> (asserts valid && complete && no errors, rehashes each analysis.txt)

fixed_harness_parameters.perf: perf record -q -e cycles:u -F 999 --call-graph dwarf,16384 (frequency/stack size are hardcoded, so they are identical across runs)
fixed_harness_parameters.heaptrack: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/heaptrack/libheaptrack_preload.so on the Rust symbolized binary only; heaptrack_interpret then heaptrack_print -m 0
fixed_harness_parameters.session_order: per case: controls first, then each mode; repetition 1 reverses the language order

artifacts.note: The baseline, Go, fixture and meter hashes were checked on 2026-10-17 and equal the identities in harness/results/perf2/profiles-final/report.json.

candidate_build.precondition: Candidate source frozen. No other owned cargo/go/test/bench jobs. Build before taking the lock; never build while a capture runs.
commands: TMPDIR=$PWD/target/tmp PB_VERSION=v0.0.0-harness PB_CLOUD_ORCHESTRATOR_AUTH_TOKEN= cargo +1.96.0 build --locked --release --target-dir target/perf3-final
TMPDIR=$PWD/target/tmp PB_VERSION=v0.0.0-harness PB_CLOUD_ORCHESTRATOR_AUTH_TOKEN= cargo +1.96.0 build --locked --profile profiling --target-dir target/perf3-profile
candidate_build.provenance: Record docs/evidence/cli-perf3/final-candidate.json in the same shape as text-candidate.json: binary paths, sha256, per-file source hashes, and build {toolchain 1.96.0, profile release|profiling, locked, PB_VERSION, PB_CLOUD_ORCHESTRATOR_AUTH_TOKEN ''}. Both binaries must come from one source hash set. Cargo.toml [profile.profiling] inherits release and only sets debug=2 and strip=none.
candidate_build.commands_are: Planning examples, not an execution transcript. Actual frozen build identities and settings are in final-candidate.json; profiling build used target/symbolized.

preflight_read_only: sha256sum bin/pb-go bin/pb-go-symbolized bin/pb-perf2-final bin/pb-perf2-final-symbolized bin/pb-perf3-final bin/pb-perf3-final-symbolized bin/pb-fixture bin/pb-meter  # compare with artifacts above
readelf -SW bin/pb-perf3-final-symbolized | grep -E '\.debug_info|\.debug_line|\.symtab'  # the harness also enforces this
pgrep -a -u "$USER" -f 'cargo|rustc|go build|harness/run.py|profile_external' || true  # must show no owned jobs
df -h .  # about 0.85 GiB per JSON run (prior profiles-final was 829M); budget about 3 GiB for all four runs

wrapping.rationale: Same lock and CPU set as docs/evidence/cli-perf2/measure.sh. Other jobs on the shared host can shift sample counts; allocation counts and contract checks are not affected.

runs.purpose: Re-capture the baseline on today's host, so the comparison does not rest only on the 2026-10-17 cli-perf2 capture
runs.command: flock -n ~/.cache/pb-rs-performance.lock taskset -c 2,4,6,8 python3 harness/profile_external.py --out harness/results/perf3/profiles-baseline-json --mode perf --mode heaptrack --case p3-100000-json --case p3-single-8MiB-item --repetitions 2 --perf-event cycles:u --go bin/pb-go-symbolized --go-release bin/pb-go --rust bin/pb-perf2-final-symbolized --rust-release bin/pb-perf2-final

flock -n ~/.cache/pb-rs-performance.lock taskset -c 2,4,6,8 python3 harness/profile_external.py --out harness/results/perf3/profiles-candidate-json --mode perf --mode heaptrack --case p3-100000-json --case p3-single-8MiB-item --repetitions 2 --perf-event cycles:u --go bin/pb-go-symbolized --go-release bin/pb-go --rust bin/pb-perf3-final-symbolized --rust-release bin/pb-perf3-final

runs.purpose: Raw-text CPU attribution for the 128KiB non-JSON SQL bridge. Both cases are existing harness cases: p3-100000-text comes from phase3_workloads, and diagnose.workload_cases derives p3-single-8MiB-text from p3-single-8MiB-item. Both are in profile_external --case choices.
runs.command: flock -n ~/.cache/pb-rs-performance.lock taskset -c 2,4,6,8 python3 harness/profile_external.py --out harness/results/perf3/profiles-candidate-text --mode perf --case p3-100000-text --case p3-single-8MiB-text --repetitions 2 --perf-event cycles:u --go bin/pb-go-symbolized --go-release bin/pb-go --rust bin/pb-perf3-final-symbolized --rust-release bin/pb-perf3-final

runs.purpose: Text runs use the reverse order (B then A), so neither binary always runs first in a host session
runs.command: flock -n ~/.cache/pb-rs-performance.lock taskset -c 2,4,6,8 python3 harness/profile_external.py --out harness/results/perf3/profiles-baseline-text --mode perf --case p3-100000-text --case p3-single-8MiB-text --repetitions 2 --perf-event cycles:u --go bin/pb-go-symbolized --go-release bin/pb-go --rust bin/pb-perf2-final-symbolized --rust-release bin/pb-perf2-final

session_accounting: Per case: controls 4 artifacts x 2 reps = 8, perf 2 languages x 2 = 4, heaptrack Rust x 2 = 2. JSON runs: 2 cases x 14 = 28. Text runs (perf only): 2 x 12 = 24. Total 104. The harness always adds controls and has no session cap flag, so these are the bounds.
optional_text_allocations: If allocation attribution of the 128KiB bridge is also wanted, add --mode heaptrack to runs 3 and 4 (+4 sessions each). This is not needed for the CPU question.

post_capture_supplementary_read_only.when: After all four runs finish, still under the lock, before any rebuild touches bin/
post_capture_supplementary_read_only.verify_first: sha256sum each perf.data against report.json samples[].profiles[0].sha256, and the binaries against report.json binaries
commands: DEBUGINFOD_URLS= perf report --stdio --children --percent-limit 2 -i harness/results/perf3/profiles-candidate-json/<case>/perf/<rep>-rust/perf.data  # inclusive call-graph view, if needed
post_capture_supplementary_read_only.scope: perf diff matches symbols by name across the two binaries. Use it only for hotspot attribution. Repeat for rep 01 and for the text runs if those were captured.

allowed: heaptrack 'calls to allocation functions' baseline vs candidate per case. Deterministic enough to compare; cli-perf2 reps differed by 170 out of 1.23M
heaptrack 'peak heap memory consumption', reported as allocator-tracked heap only, not RSS
perf self-percent symbol rankings and perf-diff deltas as hotspot attribution, with the sample population stated (cli-perf2 Go 100k had only 744 samples)
contract/output parity of every profiled session against unprofiled Go (enforced by the harness)
forbidden: Any wall time, RSS, CPU seconds or '# Samples' count from profiled sessions presented as a release speedup or memory improvement

Control rows in these reports as release timing. They are single short runs under the profiling campaign; release timing comes only from an unprofiled harness/run.py campaign of bin/pb-perf3-final vs bin/pb-perf2-final
Go heap claims from heaptrack (only Rust is preloaded; Go's managed heap is invisible to it)
PB diagnostics-feature timing sidecars (harness/diagnose.py timing modes) as performance claims

provenance_caveats: report.source is a snapshot of the working tree at capture time. For baseline runs A that is the candidate tree, not the source of pb-perf2-final-symbolized. Baseline provenance rests on the binary sha256s, which equal the cli-perf2 profiles-final binaries and docs/evidence/cli-perf3/baseline.json. State this in the write-up.
Do not edit sources between the candidate build and runs B, so the run-B source snapshot matches the candidate build's hash set.
profile_external writes with exist_ok=False. Choose fresh --out directories on every retry; never delete a failed run's directory before recording why it failed.
-F 999 and dwarf stack size are fixed in the harness. Short workloads produce small sample populations; do not raise repetitions above 2 without a new decision.
failure_handling: A non-zero exit or valid=false means stop and keep the directory. If the failure is a contract difference between candidate and Go, it is a correctness regression, not a profiling problem, and blocks the freeze.

execution.scope: These captures describe the round4 candidate. They do not describe subsequent unselected inline experiments.
